name: Snehaprava Das

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Snehaprava Das is a poet, fiction writer and translator whose work brings Odia literature into English. Her translations include Umesh Chandra Sarkar’s Padmamali and Ramshankar Ray’s Bibasini; her own poetry includes Songs of Solitude. In an interview with The Chakkar, she describes translation as a creative practice that must remain responsive to the original writer, and speaks of her interest in the workings of the mind.

Her poems here make time and memory almost tangible. “THE BORROWED MOMENT” gathers broken images to build a present, while “AUTUMN AGAIN” waits for an irretrievable moment to return. In “RAIN EVERYWHERE”, water blurs faces and portraits of the past. “BRAND ME A SINNER” adopts a more confrontational voice, rejecting the restraints of a personified Life in pursuit of an inward truth. Fragility and defiance meet across these different moods.
